subject: Clarify: Dedicated region binding, backup replication, and proof-of-deletion artifacts
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@helio-pay.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: HelioPay Security Team <security@helio-pay.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated cluster placement and deletion evidence questions

Hi Nikhil / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We are evaluating Redwood Dedicated for payment workloads and have a handful of specific questions on region pinning / backups / deletion that our auditors want answered before we proceed:  

1) If we request a region binding (US-east-1) for our Dedicated pool, can you confirm if snapshots/backups of that pool are ever replicated outside the pinned region by default?
2) What is the default retention of incremental snapshots and how do we get a certificate of deletion for snapshots and backups once requested?
3) Are system-level logs (node events, orchestration) ever replicated off-cluster or to central control-plane storage that might reside in another region?
4) If we terminate the Dedicated reservation, what is the timeline for a verified tenant wipe and what artifacts do you provide?

We'd like to collect the answers in writing for our security review. If you have a short runbook or attestation sample we can review that would be helpful.

Best,
Sofia Martinez
Head of Infrastructure Security
HelioPay

Attachment: PCI-internal-question-set.xlsx (ref)
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@helio-pay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster placement and deletion evidence questions

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear list. Below are direct answers and a proposed next step. Attaching a concise diagram and a playbook excerpt for reference.

1) Snapshots / backups: By default, snapshot storage for a region-pinned Dedicated pool is kept in-region. We do NOT geo-replicate customer snapshots unless a customer explicitly opts into cross-region replication for DR. The control plane (metadata only) may have a minimal record to index images; the actual blob stores for snapshots remain in the pinned region while the pool is active.

2) Retention and deletion certificates: Incremental snapshots are retained per the customer retention window configured at provisioning (default 30 days). Customers can request immediate snapshot purge and certified deletion. The flow: request -> scheduled purge job -> secure overwrite + metadata tombstone -> signed deletion attestation (PDF) and audit log export. Typical turnaround for attestation: 3 business days for straightforward requests, up to 7 for full forensic artifacts.

3) System logs: Node-level ephemeral logs are local to the Dedicated cluster and retained per the cluster retain window (default 7 days). Orchestration traces and higher-level control-plane events are stored in the control plane for operational reasons but we treat them as operational metadata (no user payload). For customers requiring zero-control-plane retention, we offer an opt-out where we minimize retained metadata and provide a SLA for log deletion. We'll need to confirm specific log classes if your auditors want exact retention TTLs.

4) Termination and verified wipe: On termination we perform a coordinated evacuation and cryptographic-erase workflow followed by a secondary overwrite/decommission. We provide: (a) a confirmation letter, (b) a signed wipe certificate, and (c) a sample audit log extract showing the purge and snapshot deletions. Standard timeline: 5–10 business days (accelerated options available).

Next step: I'll loop in Product Security to provide the playbook excerpts and sample artifacts. If you want a DocuSign-ready attestation, Ben can generate that once you confirm the exact wording.

Attaching: dedicated-dataflow-diagram.pdf, region-erase-playbook.pdf

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
nsharma@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster placement and deletion evidence questions

Thanks Nikhil — that's helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our auditors:  

• For (1): Can you provide a short statement confirming that snapshot blobs never leave the pinned region while the cluster exists? That statement will go in our security binder.
• For (3): When you say "control plane metadata", can you enumerate the fields retained (e.g., snapshot id, size, checksum, created_at) so we can assess whether any user-derived metadata is stored outside region?
• For (4): For the wipe certificate — will that include checksums or evidence that blob identifiers were purged, or is it a statement of process? We may request both.

If you can point us to example artifacts (even redacted) that would speed our review.

Regards,
Sofia
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@helio-pay.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster placement and deletion evidence questions

Hi Sofia — Laura from Product Security here. Quick answers and what we can deliver for your binder:  

• Snapshot residency statement (we'll provide a signed commitment letter): "While a customer-maintained Dedicated pool remains region-bound, snapshot and backup blobs are stored only in the pinned region's object store and are not geo-replicated by Redwood unless explicitly requested by the customer." We'll provide this on company letterhead and sign it.

• Control-plane metadata fields: retained fields are limited to snapshot_id, customer_id (tenant-id), size_bytes, checksum (SHA256), created_at, snapshot_ttl_days, region, and lifecycle_state. We do not store payload-level user data in the control plane. We will produce a redacted CSV extract showing field names and example non-production rows for your binder.

• Wipe certificate contents: the standard certificate includes (a) snapshot_id list, (b) timestamp of purge execution, (c) checksum values for deleted blobs (where available), (d) purge method (cryptographic-erase + overwrite), and (e) operator signature and job id. For customers that require per-blob cryptographic proof we can include signed checksums and an export of the purge job audit trail.

Deliverables we can send within 3 business days:
- Signed region-residency commitment (PDF)
- Redacted control-plane metadata CSV sample
- Sample wipe certificate (redacted)
- Region erase playbook (already attached to prior mail)

If you'd like, we can stitch these into a single DocuSign attestation package for procurement. Ben — can you create the HubSpot M-Deal record and mark the compliance package stage so we can track delivery?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Lead, Product Security
Redwood Inference
